Content: The information below is about the Marshall Plan.

:box:When World War `text(II)` ended in `1945`, Europe lay in ruins: its cities were shattered; its economies were devastated; its people faced famine. . . . To meet this emergency, Secretary of State George Marshall proposed, in a speech at Harvard University on `text(June 5, 1947)`, that European nations create a plan for their economic reconstruction and that the United States provide economic assistance. On `text(December 19, 1947)`, President Harry Truman sent Congress a message that followed Marshall’s ideas to provide economic aid to Europe. Congress overwhelmingly passed the Economic Cooperation Act of `1948`, and on `text(April 3, 1948)`, President Truman signed the act that became known as the Marshall Plan.

	Source: Public Domain/National Archives and Records Administration
